post_topic: Building CAN-SPAM compliance into an email-sending agent — HMAC tokens, suppression lists, and fail-closed design
image_description:
Single standalone diagram. One concept only. No panels, no grids, no collages. Full bleed 1080x1080px white background.

A left-to-right compliance flow diagram titled "CAN-SPAM Compliance Guard" in bold navy at the top.

The flow begins on the far left with a box labeled "Agent: Send Email Request" in navy.

An arrow points right to the first gate, a rounded rectangle labeled "Layer 1: HMAC Token Generation" in navy with a blue #5a96ff border. Inside, two smaller labels: "Input: signing key + recipient address" and "Output: signed unsubscribe token" in small gray text. A label in amber #F5A623 reads "Stateless — no DB write".

An arrow points right to a second gate, a rounded rectangle labeled "Layer 2: Suppression List Check" in navy with a blue border. Inside, label reads "Checked before every send — not at import". A downward arrow from this box leads to a small red octagon labeled "SUPPRESSED → HALT" with a red border.

An arrow continues right to a third gate, a rounded rectangle labeled "Layer 3: Physical Address Validation" in navy with a blue border. Inside, label reads "Required field: CAN-SPAM §5(a)(5)". Below it, two branching arrows: one pointing right labeled "Present → CONTINUE" in blue, and one pointing downward in amber #F5A623 leading to a box with a red border labeled "Missing → EXCEPTION RAISED → HALT" with the amber callout text "Fail-closed. Not a warning."

At the far right, a navy box labeled "Email Sent" with a checkmark, reachable only when all three layers pass.

Below the entire flow, a thin divider line, then a small label in gray: "Suppression check and address validation are gates, not filters."

Navy #0A0F1E primary elements, blue #5a96ff highlights, amber #F5A623 callouts and important labels. Clean sans-serif font. Real cloud provider logos where relevant. Small text "Kelvin Davis" bottom right corner. Professional LinkedIn infographic style similar to ByteByteGo. White background. No dark backgrounds.
